card.name: Jaipongan
card.era: Created by Gugum Gumbira; public debut 1974
card.tagline: Energetic Sundanese social dance born of cultural revival
card.profile: Jaipongan (Jaipong) is a popular Sundanese dance of West Java created by composer-choreographer Gugum Gumbira, drawing on the traditional ketuk tilu social-dance music, pencak silat martial-arts movements, and the masked Topeng Banjet theater (Wikipedia). After President Sukarno's 1961 ban on Western music and his call to revive indigenous arts, Gumbira studied rural dance and festival music for twelve years. Jaipongan made its public debut in 1974, its first known works being 'Daun Pulus Keser Bojong' and 'Rendeng Bojong.' The name imitates the sounds of the ensemble's drums. It features virtuosic kendang drumming, flirtatious singing by a sinden, and energetic hip and shoulder movements.
card.insight: Spread by the 1970s-80s cassette boom and Gumbira's Jugala orchestra - notably the 1987 album 'Tonggeret' with singer Idjah Hadidjah - Jaipongan became West Java's emblematic dance despite official concern over its sensuality (Wikipedia; Grokipedia).
